column1: # Where each file under lib/libgcc came from.
# Source of the text: runtime/udivmoddi4.c of the upstream snapshot this repository was imported from (commit
# f7bac0e, "import: upstream snapshot as received"; the file is deleted from the tree now that its text lives
# here). That file was GCC's libgcc2.c with longlong.h pasted in where libgcc2.c includes it, cut down to the
# unsigned 64-bit division functions, under five #defines that stood in for the target configuration.
# What the text is, as far as this machine can show:
#   - It is the GCC 2.7 line's. longlong.h carries "Copyright (C) 1991, 1992, 1994, 1995", names its types
#     USItype/SI_TYPE_SIZE, and knows the 2.7 set of CPUs (no alpha, sh, arc or m32r blocks).
#   - Against the FSF ChangeLog (gcc-3.3.6/gcc/FSFChangeLog.10, a local copy): libgcc2.c has the change of
#     1995-08-31 (__udivmoddi4 static inline inside the other division functions, after 2.7.0 of
#     1995-06-16); longlong.h lacks the change of 1995-10-03 (mips umul_ppmm with `l' and `h' constraints)
#     and the casts of 1997-10-18 in count_leading_zeros. A 2.7.1 or 2.7.2 release text fits that; no
#     pristine GCC 2.7 tarball is on this machine to compare with, so the release is not established.
#   - The body of __udivmoddi4 equals GCC 3.3.6's, type names aside, except for one space in a comment:
#     nobody shaped it to make it match.
# What is inferred, not read from a source:
#   - Retail's __udivdi3 and __umoddi3 are stubs that call one shared __udivmoddi4. The snapshot's text
#     cannot produce that: with its two "#if (defined (L_udivdi3) || ...)" blocks, -DL_udivdi3 compiled by
#     this toolchain inlines the whole division and makes no call. The game's libgcc was therefore built
#     from a libgcc2.c without those blocks, which is the form the file had up to 2.7.0, and they are left
#     out here. Whether the vendor's file was an older release or a changed one is not known.
#   - The three objects (_udivdi3, _udivmoddi4, _umoddi3) and their -O2 flags follow libgcc's own build,
#     one compile of libgcc2.c per function with -DL_<name>; retail's 8-byte padding between the three
#     ranges agrees with three objects.
